apod.explanation: A crescent Moon and bright Venus appear together over Poland's Tatra Mountains at dusk in a planetary conjunction, with the bright star Spica — a triple star system about 250 light-years away in Virgo — just to Venus's left.
apod.title: Moon, Venus and Spica Meet

breaking.fact: Cisco's fiscal Q1 revenue rose 24% to $18.5 billion with non-GAAP earnings of $1.40 a share, up 40%, and the company raised its fiscal 2027 revenue outlook to $74.8–75.8 billion. Applied Materials posted record Q4 revenue of $10.41 billion, up 53%, with adjusted earnings of $4.16 a share against $4.06 expected, and guided Q1 fiscal 2027 revenue to about $11.10 billion, above the $10.89 billion estimate. Cisco shares were little changed after hours; Applied Materials fell 3.6% in the regular session, then steadied after hours.
breaking.headline: Cisco and Applied Materials beat after the close on strong AI demand

breaking.fact: U.S. Antimony's Q3 revenue rose 16% to $10.1 million but missed the roughly $16.7 million estimate, and the net loss widened to $9.5 million as antimony prices fell about 63%. Gross margin expanded to 42% from 23% and antimony pounds sold rose 68%; the company projects 2026 antimony sales of 1.68–1.81 million pounds, up about 24%, with October sales of about 310,000 pounds, its best month ever. Shares fell 6.7% to $2.91 at the close and slid about 9% further after hours.
breaking.headline: U.S. Antimony's Q3 revenue misses as antimony prices plunge; shares slide after hours

breaking.fact: The S&P 500 fell 0.35% to 7,592.40, the Nasdaq 0.39% to 25,366.09 and the Dow 0.36% to 52,297.09, while the Russell 2000 dropped 1.66%. Nvidia plunged 14% at the open after Jensen Huang's resignation, then pared the loss to 4.3% at $166.19; retail investors bought about $111 million of the stock in the first half hour, the biggest opening bid on record, per Vanda Research. AMD and Broadcom each rose nearly 6% to lead S&P advancers, and energy was the best sector for a fourth straight session.
breaking.headline: Stocks close lower as Nvidia's 14% plunge outweighs energy gains

items.body: Iran's military said Thursday that four oil tankers have now been hit by explosions in the Strait of Hormuz: two supertankers carrying more than 4 million barrels combined were disabled late Wednesday after what Iran calls an unauthorised southern route — Iranian state media said they hit naval mines — and Iran's army said two more tankers hit mines Thursday afternoon in the eastern strait after disabling their radar. UKMTO separately reported a vessel hit by an unidentified projectile near Ras Al-Khaimah on Wednesday, causing an engine-room fire. Reuters could not verify Iran's account. At least 10 ships were hit in the first 10 days of November, after 37 attacks in October, per Washington Institute data.
items.headline: Four tankers struck by explosions in the Strait, Iran says

items.body: Kpler data reported by Reuters shows commercial cargo transits through the strait fell to 5 last Saturday, from 31 the week before, with none recorded Sunday, after ADNOC said three of its vessels were attacked; the IMO counts 133 confirmed incidents and 25 seafarer deaths since February, and is not advising ships to transit. Some vessels sail with AIS switched off, so the true count may be higher.
items.headline: Strait traffic collapses: 5 transits Saturday, none Sunday

hormuz.stats: Traffic & shares (latest verified): AIS-visible commercial traffic is running about 8% of normal — 6.9 ships a day over the past week (18 tankers) against 84.8 before the crisis. EIA puts Hormuz oil flows at 4.9M bbl/day in Q2 2026, down from 21.6M in Q4 2025; the IEA estimates ~20M bbl/day transited in 2025, about a quarter of global seaborne oil trade. China takes ~42% and India ~13% of strait crude throughput; ~90% of Iran's oil exports go to China. The EIA warns vessel-tracking data have become less reliable during the conflict.

marketsNote: Thursday's close: stocks ended lower after a volatile session — S&P 500 -0.35% at 7,592.40, Nasdaq -0.39%, Dow -0.36% — as Nvidia plunged 14% at the open on Jensen Huang's resignation before recovering to -4.3%, while AMD and Broadcom each rose nearly 6%. Oil jumped (WTI $88.70, Brent $95.77) after four tankers were hit in the Strait of Hormuz; the VIX rose to 18.7 and the 10-year yield topped 5% at 5.103%. After the close, Cisco and Applied Materials both beat estimates on strong AI demand, and U.S. Antimony's Q3 revenue missed; Friday brings the October PPI report.

space.body: Astronomers sifting through Vera C. Rubin Observatory data found 2026 ED138, an object 46 times farther from the Sun than Earth that takes 281 years to complete an orbit. Estimated at 370 to 930 miles across, it is likely big enough to be round and could become the solar system's sixth dwarf planet; its orbit is tilted nearly 25 degrees, suggesting a past gravitational brush with Neptune.
space.headline: Possible new dwarf planet found far beyond Pluto

space.body: NASA announced Nov 7 it has selected SpaceX to launch communications satellites aboard Starship in 2028 for its Cislunar Communications Deployment Demonstration, building the relay network for astronauts and a planned base near the Moon's south pole. The demo sits within a broader Moon Base plan for an initial constellation of five relay satellites, followed by a second constellation from another provider.
space.headline: NASA picks SpaceX to launch lunar communications satellites on Starship

space.body: University of Washington researchers, publishing Nov 12 in Science, showed that stretching and compressing magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene swings its electrical resistance by more than 100 times that of an ordinary metal, an effect amplified at very low temperatures. The new “strain knob” gives physicists a way to tune the material's exotic quantum states.
space.headline: Strain tunes magic-angle graphene resistance more than 100-fold

weekInBrief.body: Gold fell 2.96% to $3,882.10 Thursday as the 10-year Treasury yield climbed 10.5 basis points to 5.103%, its highest in weeks, after the hotter-than-expected October CPI hardened expectations of a December rate hike. The yield move also pressured rate-sensitive stocks, with the Russell 2000 down 1.66%.
weekInBrief.headline: Gold slides nearly 3% as the 10-year yield tops 5%

weekInBrief.body: The S&P 500 energy index rose for a fourth straight session as the day's best-performing sector, with refiners and LNG names leading — Valero up 3.1% and Cheniere up 1.6% — as crude rallied on the latest tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz. Energy was the one clear winner on a day the broad market fell.
weekInBrief.headline: Energy leads the market for a fourth straight session

weekInBrief.body: A regional WHO body is meeting this week to decide whether the United States has kept its measles elimination status, and STAT, The Guardian and The Hill report the country is likely to lose it. The US is in its largest measles outbreak in 35 years, with more than 5,400 cases reported; the CDC says its response is unchanged.
weekInBrief.headline: US likely to lose measles elimination status

weekInBrief.body: Axios reported, citing six senior sources, that President Trump has approved a crackdown on firms suspected of diverting Nvidia AI chips to China three times this year — in May, in August and again on November 5 — but the restrictions still have not been implemented. The report lands as Nvidia's leadership shake-up rattles chip stocks.
weekInBrief.headline: Trump approved Nvidia chip-diversion crackdown — but curbs still not in place
